## Rules

Andrew's computer checks these automatically on every push. Breaking any one
blocks the app from reaching TestFlight, and the report on the commit names the
rule and how to fix it. Never try to get around a rule: if the app truly needs
something a rule forbids, stop and use `/willoughby-apps:help` so Andrew can decide.

### The app's identity

- Your app's bundle ID is set by Andrew when he approves the app. Never change it.

### project.yml

- The app is described by `project.yml` at the top of the repo. Keep it there.
- Keep `project.yml` plain YAML: no anchors, aliases, merge keys or custom tags.
- Never add anything to `project.yml` that runs a command during a build or pulls in another file.
- Use only the `project.yml` keys the template uses.
- Only set the build settings the template already sets.
- One iPhone app target, plus at most one unit-test and one UI-test target.
- The app is iOS only.
- The app is iPhone only (TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY "1").
- The app targets iOS 18.0. Never change the deployment target.
- Swift packages only from Andrew's allowlist, pinned to an exact version. No frameworks, Carthage or local packages.
- Every path in `project.yml` stays inside the repo.

### Files in the repo

- Never commit an `.xcodeproj` or `.xcworkspace`. The build machine generates the project from `project.yml`.
- Never commit `.xcconfig` files.
- Never commit binaries or archives (.a, .dylib, .framework, .zip, compiled programs). Everything is Swift source, images and text.
- Only Swift source, images and text files. No C, Objective-C, C++, assembly or Metal files, and no other kinds of file (the allowed kinds are under Reference).
- Never commit symbolic links.
- Keep every file under 5 MB and the whole repo under 50 MB. Shrink big images.
- Never add Swift packages of your own (Package.swift), CocoaPods, Carthage, git submodules, or scanner configuration.
- Never add comments that silence a security scanner (the list is under Reference).
- Never add git filters, drivers or export settings in `.gitattributes` (the list is under Reference).

### Swift code

- No Swift macros and no package or compiler plugins.
- No loading code at run time, no calling private Apple APIs by name, and no running JavaScript text (the list is under Reference).

### Swift packages

- Every Swift package is pinned in `Package.resolved` at an allowed version.

### Capabilities

- No entitlements (capabilities like iCloud, push, HealthKit) unless Andrew has enabled them for your app.

### Privacy

- When the app uses the camera, microphone, photos, location, contacts or similar, declare the matching NS...UsageDescription in plain words.
- List every NS...UsageDescription key in README.md under Permissions, with what it is for.

### Andrew's servers

- Your app brings its own server. Never make it talk to Andrew's servers, websites, private network or home network, and never write their addresses anywhere in the repo (the list is under Reference).
- Never loosen App Transport Security (`NSAppTransportSecurity`): the app talks only to `https` servers, never plain `http` or the local network.

### Secrets

- Never put API keys, tokens or passwords in the code. If a feature needs one, stop and ask Andrew with /willoughby-apps:help.

### Security scanners

- Andrew's computer runs security scanners on every push; nothing ships until they all run.
- Andrew's computer runs security scanners on every push; anything they find blocks the release.

### Reference

**The app**

- Bundle ID starts with `com.willoughbytools.` and is set by Andrew.
- Platform `iOS`, deployment target `18.0`, `TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY: "1"` (iPhone only).
- Targets: `application` (1 to 1), `bundle.unit-test` (0 to 1), `bundle.ui-testing` (0 to 1).

**Never in `project.yml`** (at any depth)

- `aggregateTargets`: defines script-only targets
- `buildPhase`: puts files in a build phase of its choosing, including a copy to any folder on the build machine
- `buildRules`: runs a custom command on matching files during the build
- `buildScripts`: runs a shell script as a build phase
- `buildToolPlugins`: runs a Swift package build-tool plugin during the build
- `compilerFlags`: passes extra flags to the compiler for some files
- `configFiles`: points build settings at an .xcconfig file
- `copyFiles`: copies files to a destination it names, which can be any folder on the build machine
- `groups`: applies shared build-setting groups outside the checked settings
- `include`: pulls another spec file into the project
- `legacy`: hands the build to an external build tool
- `postActions`: runs a shell script after a scheme action
- `postBuildScripts`: runs a shell script after every build
- `postCompileScripts`: runs a shell script after compiling
- `postGenCommand`: runs a shell command after XcodeGen generates the project
- `preActions`: runs a shell script before a scheme action
- `preBuildScripts`: runs a shell script before every build
- `preGenCommand`: runs a shell command before XcodeGen generates the project
- `projectReferences`: references another Xcode project
- `settingGroups`: defines shared build-setting groups outside the checked settings
- `targetTemplates`: defines templates whose contents are merged in by XcodeGen
- `templates`: merges target templates into a target

**`project.yml` keys you may use**

- Top level: `name`, `options`, `settings`, `packages`, `targets`, `schemes`
- `options`: `bundleIdPrefix`, `deploymentTarget`, `developmentLanguage`, `createIntermediateGroups`, `groupSortPosition`, `generateEmptyDirectories`, `indentWidth`, `tabWidth`, `usesTabs`, `xcodeVersion`, `minimumXcodeGenVersion`
- A target: `type`, `platform`, `supportedDestinations`, `deploymentTarget`, `sources`, `resources`, `settings`, `info`, `entitlements`, `dependencies`, `scheme`
- A `sources` entry: `path`, `excludes`, `includes`, `name`, `group`, `optional`, `type`, `createIntermediateGroups`
- A target's `info` or `entitlements`: `path`, `properties`
- Target dependencies: `package`, `target`, `sdk`

**Build settings you may set**

- `ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME`, `ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_GLOBAL_ACCENT_COLOR_NAME`, `BUNDLE_LOADER`, `CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS`, `CODE_SIGN_STYLE`, `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION`, `DEVELOPMENT_ASSET_PATHS`, `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM`, `ENABLE_PREVIEWS`, `GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE`, `INFOPLIST_FILE`, `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET`, `LOCALIZATION_PREFERS_STRING_CATALOGS`, `MARKETING_VERSION`, `PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER`, `PRODUCT_NAME`, `SUPPORTS_MACCATALYST`, `SUPPORTS_MAC_DESIGNED_FOR_IPHONE_IPAD`, `SUPPORTS_XR_DESIGNED_FOR_IPHONE_IPAD`, `SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY`, `SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION`, `SWIFT_EMIT_LOC_STRINGS`, `SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY`, `SWIFT_VERSION`, `TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY`, `TEST_HOST`, `TEST_TARGET_NAME`
- Any setting starting with `INFOPLIST_KEY_`
- `SUPPORTS_MACCATALYST` must be `NO`
- `SUPPORTS_MAC_DESIGNED_FOR_IPHONE_IPAD` must be `NO`
- `SUPPORTS_XR_DESIGNED_FOR_IPHONE_IPAD` must be `NO`

**The only files you may commit**

- Text (UTF-8, no control characters): `.swift`, `.md`, `.txt`, `.json`, `.plist`, `.entitlements`, `.xcprivacy`, `.yml`, `.yaml`, `.strings`, `.stringsdict`, `.xcstrings`, `.svg`, `.csv`, and files named `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `.gitkeep`, `Package.resolved`, `LICENSE`.
- Images, which must really be that kind of image: `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.heic`, `.pdf`.
- Nothing else: no `.c`, `.m`, `.h`, `.cpp`, `.s` or `.metal` files, fonts or other data.

**Files that are never allowed**

- Anything ending in `.xcodeproj`, `.xcworkspace`, `.pbxproj`, `.xcscheme`.
- `.xcconfig` files.
- Binaries and archives: `.a`, `.o`, `.so`, `.dylib`, `.framework`, `.xcframework`, `.bundle`, `.swiftmodule`, `.car`, `.app`, `.appex`, `.ipa`, `.exe`, `.dll`, `.jar`, `.class`, `.zip`, `.tar`, `.gz`, `.tgz`, `.bz2`, `.xz`, `.7z`, `.rar`, `.dmg`, `.pkg`, `.deb`, `.rpm`, or any file that is really one of: 7-zip archive, ELF executable, ar archive (static library), bzip2 archive, compress (.Z) archive, cpio archive, cpio archive (odc), gzip archive, lz4 archive, lzip archive, mach-o 32-bit, mach-o 32-bit (swapped), mach-o 64-bit, mach-o 64-bit (swapped), rar archive, tar archive, universal binary, universal binary (swapped), universal binary 64-bit, wasm module, xar archive (.pkg, .xip), xz archive, zip archive, zstd archive, or that opens as a zip archive.
- Any file over 5 MB, a repo over 50 MB, or more than 5,000 files.
- Symbolic links.
- `.gitleaks.toml`: changes what the secret scanner looks for
- `.gitleaksignore`: tells the secret scanner to ignore findings
- `.gitmodules`: pulls another repository into this one
- `.osv-scanner.toml`: tells the vulnerability scanner to ignore findings
- `.semgrepignore`: tells the code scanner to skip files
- `.swiftpm`: holds Swift package manager configuration
- `Cartfile`: uses Carthage, which fetches prebuilt binaries
- `Package.swift`: defines a Swift package, which can carry plugins and macros that run during the build
- `Podfile`: uses CocoaPods, which runs scripts during install
- `osv-scanner.toml`: tells the vulnerability scanner to ignore findings
- The text `gitleak` directly followed by `s:allow`, anywhere: it silences the secret scanner on that line
- The text `nos` directly followed by `em:`, anywhere: it silences the code scanner on that line
- The text `nose` directly followed by `mgrep`, anywhere: it silences the code scanner on that line
- In `.gitattributes`, setting any of: `filter`, `diff`, `merge`, `export-subst`, `export-ignore`, `ident`, `working-tree-encoding` (`-name` to unset one is fine).

**Swift code that is never allowed**

- Code that imports a compiler or package plugin library (pattern `^\s*import\s+(PackagePlugin|SwiftCompilerPlugin|SwiftSyntaxMacros|SwiftSyntax|SwiftSyntaxBuilder)\b`).
- Code that declares a Swift macro backed by a compiler plugin (pattern `#externalMacro\b`).
- Code that implements a Swift package or compiler plugin (pattern `\b(BuildToolPlugin|CommandPlugin|CompilerPlugin|XcodeBuildToolPlugin)\b`).
- Code that loads native code at run time (dlopen/dlsym) (pattern `\b(dlopen|dlsym)\b`), even in a comment.
- Code that loads a code bundle at run time (pattern `\bBundle\(\s*(path|url):[^)]*\)\??\s*\.(load|loadAndReturnError)\b`), even in a comment.
- Code that binds a Swift name to an arbitrary C symbol (@_silgen_name), a way to call dlopen or private functions unseen (pattern `@_silgen_name\b`), even in a comment.
- Code that looks up a class or method by a string name, the usual way to call private Apple APIs (pattern `\b(NSClassFromString|NSSelectorFromString)\b`), even in a comment.
- Code that runs JavaScript text, which can come from the network and change what the app does after review (pattern `\b(evaluateScript|evaluateJavaScript|callAsyncJavaScript|WKUserScript)\b`), even in a comment.

**Allowed Swift packages** (pinned in `Package.resolved`)

- None yet. Every feature is built with Apple's own frameworks.

**Entitlements Andrew has enabled**

- None for any app yet.

**Privacy keys** (declare it in `project.yml` as `INFOPLIST_KEY_<key>`, and list it in `README.md`)

| When the app uses | Declare |
|---|---|
| the camera | `NSCameraUsageDescription` |
| the microphone | `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` |
| the whole photo library | `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` |
| saving photos to the library | `NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription` |
| location | `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription` |
| contacts | `NSContactsUsageDescription` |
| the calendar | `NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription` |
| speech recognition | `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` |
| Health data | `NSHealthShareUsageDescription` |
| motion and fitness | `NSMotionUsageDescription` |
| Bluetooth | `NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription` |
| Face ID | `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` |
| cross-app tracking | `NSUserTrackingUsageDescription` |
| the music library | `NSAppleMusicUsageDescription` |
| NFC | `NFCReaderUsageDescription` |

**Addresses never allowed anywhere in the repo** (any capitals, in code, settings, resources or docs)

- Andrew's own domain (`willoughbytools` then `.xyz`) and every address under it (pattern `willoughbytools\.xyz\b`).
- An Amazon API Gateway address (`<id>.execute-api.<region>.amazonaws` then `.com`), where Andrew's APIs live (pattern `\b[a-z0-9]+\.execute-api\.[a-z0-9-]+\.amazonaws\.com\b`).
- An AWS Lambda function address (`<id>.lambda-url.<region>.on` then `.aws`), where Andrew's services live (pattern `\b[a-z0-9]+\.lambda-url\.[a-z0-9-]+\.on\.aws\b`).
- A Tailscale address (anything ending in `.ts` then `.net`), Andrew's private network (pattern `\b[a-z0-9-]+\.ts\.net\b`).
- A Tailscale IP address (100.64 to 100.127, then two more numbers) (pattern `(?<![\d.])100\.(?:6[4-9]|[7-9]\d|1[01]\d|12[0-7])\.\d{1,3}\.\d{1,3}(?![\d])`).
- A home-network IP address (192.168, then two more numbers) (pattern `(?<![\d.])192\.168\.\d{1,3}\.\d{1,3}(?![\d])`).
- A private-network IP address (10, then three more numbers) (pattern `(?<![\d.])10\.\d{1,3}\.\d{1,3}\.\d{1,3}(?![\d])`).
- A private-network IP address (172.16 to 172.31, then two more numbers) (pattern `(?<![\d.])172\.(?:1[6-9]|2\d|3[01])\.\d{1,3}\.\d{1,3}(?![\d])`).
- This computer (`local` then `host`, or 127 then three more numbers), which on a phone is nothing and on a build machine is Andrew's (pattern `(?<![\d.])127\.\d{1,3}\.\d{1,3}\.\d{1,3}(?![\d])|\blocalhost\b`).
- A link-local IP address (169.254, then two more numbers): a router, a printer, or a cloud machine's own metadata service (pattern `(?<![\d.])169\.254\.\d{1,3}\.\d{1,3}(?![\d])`).
- The any-address (four zeros joined by dots), which reaches this device's own servers (pattern `(?<![\d.])0\.0\.0\.0(?![\d.])`).
- A home-network name ending in `.local` (Bonjour), such as the Mini's or Home Assistant's, written in quotes, after `//`, `@`, `=` or `>`, or with a hyphen in its first part (pattern `(?:(?<=["'/@>=])|(?<![\w.-])(?=[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+\.))[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?(?:\.[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?)*\.local\.?(?![\w-]|\.[a-z0-9])`).
- A web address whose server name has no dot (a bare machine name, which a phone looks up on whatever private network it is on, Andrew's tailnet included) (pattern `(?<![\w+.-])(?:https?|wss?|ftp)://(?:[^\s/?#@"'<>]*@)?(?!local[h]ost(?![\w-]))(?!0x[0-9a-f]+(?=[:/?#"'<>\s)\]]|$))(?=[a-z0-9_-]*[a-z_-])[a-z0-9_-]+(?=[:/?#"'<>\s)\]]|$)`).
- A web address whose server is a number not written as four plain numbers from 0 to 255 joined by dots (one big number, hex, octal or a shortened form), which is how a private address hides (pattern `(?<![\w+.-])(?:https?|wss?|ftp)://(?:[^\s/?#@"'<>]*@)?(?!(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|1\d\d|[1-9]?\d)(?=[:/?#"'<>\s)\]]|$))(?:0x[0-9a-f]+|\d+)(?:\.(?:0x[0-9a-f]+|\d+)){0,3}(?=[:/?#"'<>\s)\]]|$)`).
- A private or link-local IPv6 address (starting fc, fd, or fe8 to feb, then colons): every Tailscale device has one, starting fd7a then 115c (pattern `(?<![\w:.])f(?:[cd][0-9a-f]{2}|e[89ab][0-9a-f])(?::[0-9a-f]{0,4}){2,7}(?![\w:])`).
- This device in IPv6 (two colons then 1, its long form, or two colons in square brackets) or an IPv4 address written as IPv6 (two colons then ffff) (pattern `(?<![\w:])(?::[:]1(?![\w:])|(?:0{1,4}:){7}0{0,3}1(?![\w:])|:[:]ffff:(?=[0-9a-f])|(?:0{1,4}:){5}ffff:(?=[0-9a-f]))|\[:[:]\]`).

**Scanners run on every push**

- `gitleaks`: secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords)
- `osv-scanner`: dependencies with known vulnerabilities
- `semgrep`: risky Swift code (downloaded code, private APIs, script injection)
- `clamscan`: known malware signatures
